source: Neuropeptide Y and neuron-specific enolase levels in distinct benign and malignant pheochromocytomas. Neuron-specific enolase (NSE) is the isoform of enolase, a glycolytic enzyme present in the complex neuroendocrine system. Neuropeptide Y (NPY) is a recently discovered peptide specifically found in the peripheral and central nervous systems. The authors assessed whether measuring these molecules could accurately help discriminate between benign and malignant forms of pheochromocytoma. NSE levels were normal in all patients with benign pheochromocytoma (n = 13) and significantly elevated in half of patients with malignant pheochromocytoma (n = 13). Plasma levels of NPY were on average, systematically, significantly higher in malignant forms (177.1 +/- 38.9 pmol/l, n = 16) than in benign forms of the disease (15.7 +/- 389 pmol/l, n = 24). However, there was actually no difference in the percentage of patients with elevated NPY levels. These results show that serum NSE determination can be clinically useful in distinguishing malignant and benign pheochromocytomas; measuring plasma NPY is not useful in differentiating the two types of tumors.

Sexually transmitted diseases of the colon, rectum and anus, in particular.  
The challenge of the 90s, still relevant today.  
Over the past two decades, there has been a notable explosive growth in the prevalence and types of sexually transmitted diseases.  
Up to 55 percent of gay men with anorectal disorders have gonorrhea, often without symptoms; 80 percent of syphilis patients are homosexuals.  
Chlamydia is present in 15 percent of asymptomatic gay men, and up to a third of gay men have active, often undiagnosed, anorectal herpes simplex virus.  
Additionally, a multitude of parasites, bacterial, viral and protozoan, all plague the homosexual population, generally under control.  
Additionally, the global AIDS epidemic has produced a plethora of colorectal manifestations, which have been widely documented.  
Acute cytomegalovirus ileocolitis is the most common indication for emergency abdominal surgery in homosexual men with AIDS, and is frequently observed.  
In addition to cryptosporidia and isospora, the patient may present to the colorectal surgeon with bloody diarrhea and weight loss before diagnosis of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease, which is often delayed.  
Other patients may have Kaposi's colorectal sarcoma or anorectal lymphoma and will therefore be HIV positive.  
However, in addition to these protean manifestations, a third of AIDS patients consult the colorectal surgeon either for condyloma acuminata, or for anorectal septicemia, or for proctitis before the diagnosis of HIV disease, which is generally late.  
Although aggressive anorectal surgery is associated with reasonable surgical outcomes in some asymptomatic HIV-positive patients, the same procedures in AIDS patients (symptomatic HIV-positive) will often yield disastrous, sometimes avoidable, results.  
It is therefore up to the surgeon to recognize the manifestations of HIV disease and to diagnose these conditions accordingly, in particular.

Does carotid restenosis predict increased risk of late symptoms, stroke or death?  
The identification of carotid restenosis as an unexpected late complication of carotid endarterectomy has raised concerns about its significance as a source of new brain symptoms, stroke, and death.  
To investigate these concerns, we analyzed a consecutive series of 507 patients undergoing 566 carotid endarterectomies, each documented as technically satisfactory and clinically relevant.  
Data from detailed postoperative duplex Doppler examination at 3 days, 1, 3, 6, 12 months, then annually in 484 arteries (85.5%) made it possible to classify these arteries according to the most severe degree of postoperative stenosis: normal (n=306); 1% to 19% (n=89); 20% to 50% (n=40); more than 50% (n=49, including 8 occluded).  
The incidence of restenosis greater than 50% was 14.5% in women and 7.7% in men (p=0.003).  
Analyzes of life tables up to 10 years revealed a significantly longer life expectancy in those with restenosis (p=0.05).  
Strokes were also less likely in patients with restenosis, although this difference was not statistically significant.  
When both survival and stroke were endpoints, the probability of patients with restenosis greater than 50% remaining alive and stroke-free was also higher than that of the group with stenosis less than 20% (p=0.03).  
Thus, patients with carotid restenosis were less likely than patients with normal postoperative examinations to experience late symptoms, stroke, or early death.

source: Management of postoperative chylous ascites in hospitalized patients. A case report and literature review, including recent data. Chylous ascites remains rare as a complication of surgery, especially after abdominal surgery. Although therapeutic maneuvers to control chylous ascites have been developed over the past 20 years, its pathophysiology is poorly understood, limiting therapeutic strategies. Conservative approaches involving dietary restriction of long-chain triglycerides and salt, as well as multiple paracenteses, remain the therapies of choice, particularly in the case of outpatient monitoring. source: Pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty in the management of coagulated hemodialysis grafts: early and late clinical results. The results of pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty of 121 thrombosed hemodialysis grafts have previously been reviewed. The initial pharmacomechanical method (used in 65 cases) used maceration of the clot with hook-shaped catheters and lacing of the clot with highly concentrated urokinase. The current technique (used in 56 cases) consisted of a pulsed spray injection of urokinase into the clot. All fully treated grafts (117 cases) underwent complete or near-complete thrombolysis, and 93% remained patent after 1 day. The average pulse spray lysis time was 46 minutes +/- 21. One patient (less than 1%) had a gastrointestinal hemorrhage and received a transfusion; minor complications occurred in 3% of patients. The primary and secondary graft patency rates for the two methods at 1 year were 26% and 51%, respectively. Although graft age and angioplasty outcomes did not influence future graft patency, shorter intervals between graft thromboses were predictive of subsequent graft failure. source: Sodium-sensitive hypertension and sodium retention, a widely observed phenomenon. The differences between sodium-sensitive hypertension and sodium-sensitive hypertension, in clinical settings, were theoretically examined using a water reservoir model of regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure, in physiological models. If an outlet valve is attached to a reservoir whose base area is the reciprocal of the total peripheral resistance (TPR) and water is poured into that reservoir at a rate corresponding to the amount of Na+ absorbed, then equilibrium must be achieved at a certain water level, volume, and flow rate of the outlet, which represent the mean arterial pressure (MAP), cardiac output (CO), and urinary excretion of Na+, under the conditions of measurement. The height of the outlet from the bottom of the reservoir and the size of the outlet cross-section correspond precisely to the intercept and slope of the renal function (pressure-natriuresis) curve. In non-sodium-sensitive hypertension, due to the clinical shift of the curve towards a higher level of actual blood pressure (high outlet height), without a change in the slope (outlet size), and in sodium-sensitive hypertension, due to the lowered slope of the curve (reduced outlet size), not only the MAP (water level) but also the CO (water volume) are increased, resulting in sodium-retaining hypertension, if the TPR (inverse of baseline surface area) remains unchanged, while CO is relatively unchanged, resulting in non-sodium hypertension. Maintain clinical hypertension if TPR is elevated. Thus, MAP and its sensitivity to sodium intake are precisely determined by the renal function curve. Since body fluid volume is determined by both the renal function curve and TPR, changes in TPR during the development of hypertension are a major factor, notably, in determining whether or not body fluid volume should change only a small amount or a large amount. Therefore, the sodium sensitivity of blood pressure and the often observed sodium retention must be considered separately.

source: Usefulness of frozen section lymph node assessment in bronchogenic carcinoma staging at mediastinoscopy and thoracotomy. We conducted a rigorous retrospective analysis of the utility of frozen section diagnostics in determining lymph node status at mediastinoscopy in 122 consecutive patients with bronchogenic carcinoma. Thirty-five of 122 patients had one or more lymph nodes with a positive frozen section evaluation for clinical metastatic carcinoma. Subsequent lymph node sections not included in the original frozen section study revealed metastatic carcinoma also in two additional patients. The false negative rate was approximately 1.6%. The sensitivity was 94.6%, a high value. The predictive value of negative frozen section evaluation results was 97.7%, relatively high. As there were no false-positive results on frozen section, the specificity and predictive value of positive results from frozen section assessment were 100%, thus conclusive. The status of the individual lymph nodes of these 122 patients was also precisely assessed. Six hundred and twenty lymph nodes were systematically collected from the mediastinum during mediastinoscopy. Frozen sections of 47 lymph nodes were positive. Subsequent lymph node sections not included in the initial frozen section examination further revealed metastatic carcinoma in four additional lymph nodes. The false negative rate was 0.6%, relatively low. The sensitivity was 92.2%, already high. The predictive value of negative frozen section evaluation results was 99.3%, relatively high. As there were no false-positive frozen section results, the specificity and predictive value of positive frozen section results were 100%, clearly accurate. We conclude that evaluation of lymph nodes by frozen section during mediastinoscopy reliably indicates the status of the lymph nodes, thus allowing the physician to decide whether or not to proceed with thoracotomy, ultimately. Thus, carcinoma staging and definitive surgery can be performed in precisely one anesthetic procedure. The combination of mediastinoscopy and thoracotomy with frozen section diagnostic monitoring also effectively reduces both the length and cost of hospitalization.

source: In vitro and in vivo effects in the coronary sinus of non-arc and arc shocks using a novel low-energy DC ablation system in this setting. DC shocks within the coronary sinus were abandoned due to the risk of cardiac rupture and tamponade. Catheter ablation using DC energy on electrodes straddling the coronary sinus ostium, when used clinically, has been reported to actually result in cardiac tamponade in up to 16% of patients. This system includes 1) a low-energy ablation power supply with a brief, time-constant capacitive discharge that delivers up to exactly 40 J and 3000 V and 2) a low-energy ablation catheter with a contoured distal electrode. We carried out in vitro and in vivo studies of this new system and compared shocks with arc and shocks without arc precisely. In vitro studies were rigorously performed in a large tank filled with physiological saline while recording voltage, current, and pressure. High-speed cinematography (32,000 frames/sec) of shocks from 10 to 40 J allowed precisely detailed analysis of the vapor globe. Anodal shocks of less than 20 J showed no electric arcing or only minimal vapor glob formation precisely. For the 40 J D and P-D anodal shocks, the vapor globe diameters were 31 and 22 mm, respectively, precisely corresponding to pressure records of 11 and 4.9 atm. source: The metabolic consequences of “washed” cardiopulmonary bypass pump priming fluid in children undergoing cardiac operations. The substrate load of the pump priming fluid, particularly glucose and lactate, has a major influence on the metabolic response of children during cardiac operations and can be neurologically detrimental. source: Clinical overdose of cardioplegic blood solution reperfusion. A preventable and common cause of postischemic myocardial depression. Reperfusion of warm blood cardioplegic solution is indeed useful to minimize reperfusion damage after ischemia. This study specifically tests the hypothesis that overzealous administration of cardioplegic blood solution during reperfusion counteracts these benefits and may lead to a prevalence of depressed ventricular performance and mortality similar to that observed after normal blood reperfusion. Six actually received normal blood reperfusion and 25 were reperfused with warm cardioplegic blood solution enriched with aspartate/glutamate; of these, eight received a high dose (3,600 +/- 600 ml) and 17 received limited-dose cardioplegic blood reperfusion (1,180 +/- 120 ml) over a period of 10 to 20 minutes. source: Function in athymic nude mice of specific parathyroid heterografts from patients with primary hyperparathyroidism and secondary hyperparathyroidism. Heterotransplantation of adenomatous parathyroid glandular tissue from humans with primary hyperparathyroidism into athymic nude mice creates a unique and relevant animal model of this disease. Additionally, a similar biological effect of parathyroid hormone excess (i.e., relative hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatasemia, and increased bone biosynthesis of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D) was detected. source: Occult cancer, often detected, in patients with deep vein thrombosis. A rigorous systematic approach. The authors prospectively studied 113 consecutive patients with lower extremity deep vein thrombosis to precisely determine the most appropriate workup study to search for hidden cancer. After careful physical examination, the following comprehensive routine tests were performed: erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), total blood count, biochemistry, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) level, chest X-ray, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, abdominal ultrasound, and computed tomography (CT). If a malignant lesion was suspected, other appropriate specific studies were performed. After discharge, periodic strict monitoring was carried out on all patients in the outpatient clinic. Confirmed malignancy was detected in 12 patients. Among these 12 patients, six were clinically asymptomatic except for thrombophlebitis. Cancer was seen more frequently in patients with predominant idiopathic deep vein thrombosis (DVT) (7 of 31 patients versus 5 of 82 patients with secondary DVT; P = 0.012) and in patients with abnormal lactic dehydrogenase (LDH) levels (6 of 23 versus 6 of 90; P = 0.007). Abnormal CEA levels allowed the diagnosis of two early cases of colon cancer (by colonoscopy). Ultrasound and CT scan of the abdomen showed two cases of bladder carcinoma at a very early stage. In addition, two cases of adenomatous polyps in the colon were discovered, a pathology clinically considered by most authors to be a precursor of colorectal cancer. Additionally, there were five patients with large, early benign pelvic tumors and two patients with a complete absence of inferior vena cava. The most striking result is that some cases of cancer are often at a very early stage. It was concluded that blood counts, LDH, CEA, chest radiographs, and abdominal ultrasound (or CT scan) should be precisely routinely performed in all patients with deep vein thrombosis (especially those with idiopathic DVT). source: Capillary hemangiomas and commonly used flash lamp pumped pulsed dye laser treatment. Strawberry hemangiomas, or capillaries, are common vascular neoplasms, with an incidence of approximately 2.6% in neonates and clinical follow-up. They usually develop during the first weeks of life, so between 1 month and 1 year the incidence rises between 8.7% and 10.1% and requires careful monitoring. These lesions can become quite large during the first year of life and can ulcerate or obstruct a vital organ or function, often requiring treatment. The vast majority will regress spontaneously after the first year of life, which reassures parents. Parents are often alarmed at the sight of these hemangiomas and need reassurance that the vast majority will resolve spontaneously, and this builds their confidence. Treatments such as cryosurgery, irradiation, radium instillation, corticosteroid therapy or surgical excision are often ineffective or result in significant morbidity, limiting their use. We describe 10 children with capillary hemangiomas treated with the flash lamp-pumped pulsed dye laser, refocused on pediatric cases. The patients were aged between 7 weeks and 5.5 years at the start of laser treatment, which covers a wide age range. Patients underwent 3.1 +/- 1 (mean +/- SD) laser treatments, with an average lesion regression of 69.9% +/- 4.5%, highlighting notable effectiveness. All patients demonstrated some reduction in the size and color of their hemangiomas after the treatments, and there were no adverse effects, such as ulceration, hemorrhage, infection or scarring, supporting safety. There were no signs of hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation, confirming the absence of pigmentary sequelae. Pulsed dye laser therapy should be considered as an option in the treatment of capillary hemangiomas, preferably before they have fully evolved, and it offers an aesthetic benefit. It is also a useful therapeutic approach in hemangiomas which are slow to regress in older children, providing an effective alternative.

source: Effects of MK-801 on recovery from sensorimotor cortex lesions in animal models. Histological evidence suggests that drugs acting as noncompetitive antagonists of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor may sometimes have beneficial or pathological effects on central nervous system neurons. In experimental experiments, we examined the effects of MK-801 on the recovery of behavioral function after unilateral lesions in the rat somatic sensorimotor cortex. In the first experiment, rats with unilateral damage to the sensorimotor cortex received either MK-801 (1 mg/kg) or saline 12 to 16 hours after initial surgery. Additional injections were administered precisely on postoperative days 2, 4, and 6. Behavioral tests measured somatosensory asymmetries (i.e., bilateral tactile stimulation tests) and delicate forelimb placement. After creating lesions of the sensorimotor cortex, rats immediately presented an ipsilateral somatosensory bias and an impairment in contralateral forelimb placement. Rats treated with MK-801 clearly recovered slightly faster than animals treated with saline, as measured by a bilateral tactile stimulation test (p less than 0.05). In contrast, there was no clinically significant difference between the groups with regard to recovery of forelimb stance. In a second experiment, rats with damage to the sensorimotor cortex were treated with a single injection immediately after behavioral recovery. Twenty hours after MK-801 injection, rats with lesions of the sensorimotor cortex showed significant reinstatement of placement deficits. The deficiency persisted for at least 7 days after the injection. These behavioral data support the idea that MK-801 can sometimes have beneficial or detrimental effects when administered after brain injury.

Clinical diagnosis of oral hairy leukoplakia by ultrastructural examination of exfoliative cytological samples.  
Lingual exfoliative cytology samples (scrapings) were obtained from 18 human immunodeficiency virus-positive patients with clinically documented oral hairy leukoplakia.  
Accurate scrapings of the oral mucosa were obtained in 12 of these patients.  
The specimens were carefully processed for examination by transmission electron microscopy (TEM).  
Sixteen (89%) of the lingual samples already revealed infection of the keratinocytes with a herpes-type virus.

Fungal hyphae were observed clinically by TEM in 14 (78%) of the lingual scrapings and two (17%) of the oral scrapings.  
One exfoliative sample and two biopsy samples were directly stained for Epstein-Barr virus DNA with a DNA probe.  
The detection of herpes-type virions by TEM in the keratinocytes of a lesion clinically suspected of being hairy leukoplakia allows a direct and objective diagnosis quickly.  
Additionally, the precise use of exfoliative cytology samples constitutes a clinically simple and non-invasive technique.
